title: Group bar widgets on shared ovals
head: 5c7cccbfe0fb
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Grouped-widget insets do not track a live change of [spacing] scale or [font] base-size
leads.consequence: Changing the shell TOML spacing/font scale changes groupPad, groupGap and groupCrossInset, but none of their change signals calls scheduleGroups. Existing leadInset/trailInset retain the previous values; later redraws use the new groupPad in groupSpans, so the oval no longer matches its slots and gaps until a widget hides/reappears or the layout is rebuilt. This applies in both orientations and the anchored center copies. Trigger: group two widgets, change [spacing] scale through the watched user shell.toml or switch themes. Suggested fix: reschedule insets when groupPad or groupGap changes and rectangles when groupCrossInset or cross-axis size changes.

leads.summary: The new group tests still pass when hidden widgets are included in all four QML group filters
leads.consequence: All new behavioral assertions pass against model functions supplied already-filtered arrays and text-presence checks. A mutant that replaces every `filter(slot => slot.shown)` in the production QML with unconditional inclusion passed the complete bar-test.sh (verified, exit 0). A hidden widget can therefore continue influencing group boundaries/oval spans without triggering a test failure. Add a QML integration test with a widget that hides then reappears, or exercise the actual QML slot collector rather than only the helpers.

leads.summary: Open PR #13139 implements another grouped pill around the same slots; resolving its Bar.qml merge conflicts requires coordinating both grouping systems
leads.consequence: #13139 and this PR are diverged. A three-way merge with #13139's own base and head yields 13 conflict regions in Bar.qml, including both center groupHost/pillRun wiring, anchored clock placement and ModuleSlot padding/Loader anchors; leaving conflict markers prevents QML from loading. Even a manual resolution that simply retains both padding systems would place both pill and oval backgrounds on the same widget run when `bar.pills` is enabled. Resolve the two features and their tests together, or explicitly define their coexistence/mutual exclusion. The runtime appearance after a deliberate manual resolution has not been tested.

leads.summary: Open PR #6961's collapsible group implementation conflicts with both group-enabled ModuleList positioners
leads.consequence: #6961 is not stacked on this PR. The three-way merge using #6961's own base and head produces two conflicts in Bar.qml's Row/Column: this PR replaces them with an Item wrapping a positioner and passes `list: moduleListRoot`; #6961 passes `draggable: moduleListRoot.draggable` to nested group slots. Choosing one side alone either drops the oval slot registration/geometry or the nested-group drag guard; retain both in a coordinated resolution. Its existing mergeable state on GitHub is CONFLICTING even before considering this PR.

issues.requirement: Readable comments: each visible defect has a heading, 2-4 sentences of mechanism and Impact, and one Suggested change sentence.
issues.excerpt:
### Overlap with #13139

#13139 edits this code and ends pill runs where `"group"` changes; after it, this PR's `Bar.qml` has 13 conflicting hunks.
issues.correction: This visible finding has only one sentence of mechanism and states no Impact, so the reader cannot tell why a differing `group` meaning matters. Add a short Impact sentence, for example that the two PRs would give `group` different meanings, and cut the same number of characters elsewhere to stay within 1,500. The visible length is already 1,496. Possible cuts are shortening the Outcome clause or the second sentence of "Padding ignores live text size".

retro:
# RETRO t3-13570-47c40694

- Worked: Sol finished in 9.6 min, and its two behavioural leads matched Opus findings 2 and M9 independently. Its #13139 conflict lead was concrete and verifiable with `git merge-file` on blobs fetched through `gh api`, without touching the shared git objects.
- Friction: the 1,500-character visible budget took four trim passes. The two fixed blocks (the Community disclaimer and the AI process line) use about 560 characters, which leaves roughly 900 for three findings. Keeping a short "draft-template + verbatim reproducer insertion" script from the start worked well and made re-measuring cheap.
- Friction: the editorial checker flagged sandbox paths in a reproducer's diff header. Reviewers should write mutation diffs with `a/` and `b/` paths from the start, so coordinators don't have to redact pasted reproducers.
- Friction: `pi_job.py wait` prints `recent_tools`, which before release showed fragments of hunter activity (a reproducer name and grep terms). The fragments were not acted on, but the pre-release output could hide tool arguments completely.
- The Opus self-check was useful: 5 real qualifier losses were caught (the rebuild condition, the merge-base versus `quattro` baseline, "CLI traced in source only", the 30 px widget assumption, and hidden-only collapse).
